item.title: Insurance firm posts $7.85m profit
item.description: General insurance provider Sun Insurance Company Limited has recorded a profit before tax of $7.85 million for the six months ended June 30 this year. That is an 11 per cent increase over the corresponding period last year, reflecting continued business growth and execution of its strategic priorities.
item.content:encoded:
General insurance provider Sun Insurance Company Limited has recorded a profit before tax of $7.85 million for the six months ended June 30 this year.

That is an 11 per cent increase over the corresponding period last year, reflecting continued business growth and execution of its strategic priorities.

This is the second year that the company has been listed on the South Pacific Stock Exchange (SPX).

In its market announcement to the SPX, the company reported its insurance revenue grew to $27.02m, an increase of 21 per cent over the first half of the previous year, which it said demonstrated continued momentum across its core insurance operations.

Company chairperson Padam Lala said those results were supported by sustained premium growth, disciplined underwriting, prudent expense management, and ongoing operational improvements, enabling the delivery of higher earnings while maintaining a conservative approach to risk management.

“Our half-year performance demonstrates the resilience of our business and the commitment of our people,” Mr Lala said.

“We continue to invest responsibly, strengthen our operations and pursue opportunities that enhancer the company’s long-term value.

“We sincerely thank our customers, shareholders, employees and business partners for their continued confidence and support.”

Mr Lala said during the period, the company also further strengthened its financial position, with total assets increasing by 14.63 per cent to $149.9m, which he added reflected continued growth in their investment portfolio and disciplined capital management.

“This strong capital position provides the flexibility to invest in future growth opportunities while continuing to meet policyholder obligations.”

He said the company remained committed to expanding their property investment portfolio as part of their long-term strategy – with recent strategic property acquisitions and development projects expected to diversify earnings, increase recurring income streams, enhance the value of their asset base, and support future profitability.

Mr Lala said investor confidence had also continued to strengthen.

As at July 31 this year, Sun Insurance’s market capitalisation has grown to $386.4m, which he said showed the confidence of investors in their financial performance, governance framework and strategic direction.

“Supported by a clear strategic vision, a growing investment portfolio, and a resilient core insurance business, Sun Insurance is well positioned to capitalise on future opportunities and deliver consistent returns over the long term.”

item.title: Chinese language to be taught in schools
item.description: THE Ministry of Education is set to introduce a Chinese language pilot program in 12 schools in the Central Division, as Fiji strengthens educational cooperation with China. The program will involve six primary and six secondary schools and will introduce students to the Chinese language and culture while creating opportunities for greater cultural exchange and international learning.
item.content:encoded:
THE Ministry of Education is set to introduce a Chinese language pilot program in 12 schools in the Central Division, as Fiji strengthens educational cooperation with China.

The program will involve six primary and six secondary schools and will introduce students to the Chinese language and culture while creating opportunities for greater cultural exchange and international learning.

The initiative was discussed last week during a meeting between Education Minister Aseri Radrodro, the Director of the Chinese Language Education Centre and representatives of the Chinese Embassy.

The discussions also covered the development of learning materials, teacher training, and opportunities for students to access scholarships and other Chinese language programs.

Representatives of the Chinese Embassy expressed their willingness to support the initiative through teacher training, learning resources and other areas of co-operation.

Mr Radrodro welcomed the proposed program, saying additional language skills would help broaden educational opportunities for students and strengthen people-to-people links between Fiji and China.

item.title: Archbishop’s unity call across denominations
item.description: DENOMINATIONAL differences have at times caused division in Fiji’s villages and even within families, despite faith being rooted in unity, says head of the Catholic Church Archbishop Peter Loy Chong. He made the comment following a significant moment at Tubou, Lakeba, in Lau over the weekend, where representatives of different Christian denominations joined the Catholic community to mark 182 years
item.content:encoded:
DENOMINATIONAL differences have at times caused division in Fiji’s villages and even within families, despite faith being rooted in unity, says head of the Catholic Church Archbishop Peter Loy Chong.

He made the comment following a significant moment at Tubou, Lakeba, in Lau over the weekend, where representatives of different Christian denominations joined the Catholic community to mark 182 years since the arrival of the first Catholic missionaries in Fiji.

“The unfortunate thing now is that the different denominations have become the cause of division in villages and even in families,” Archbishop Loy Chong said.

Representatives from the Methodist Church, Christian Mission Fellowship, Assemblies of God and the Seventh-day Adventist Church attended the gathering.

Archbishop Loy Chong said the denominations were intentionally invited, reflecting the importance of sharing major occasions with the wider community.

“We wanted them to be part of the celebration,” he said.

He said the gesture reflected the traditional Fijian way of life, where communities came together to share important events.

“It’s only the Fijian way of life that you invite other people into the celebration,” he said.

Archbishop Loy Chong said many villages now had multiple denominations, making it important for churches to create opportunities to unite despite differences.

“So we encourage different churches to come together, at least once a month to worship together.”

He said such efforts would allow churches to maintain their traditions while strengthening relationships within communities.

Archbishop Loy Chong said diversity was a reality, but unity required deliberate effort.

“Diversity is a fact of the matter with the different denominations and even religions.

“But also in the diversity, we have to find ways on how to be united, to come together for something, for prayer.”

He said the Lakeba gathering demonstrated how churches could come together despite differences.

The 182nd anniversary celebrations were also attended by the Tui Nayau, Ratu Tevita Uluilakeba Mara. Events included the opening of gates to a landmark honouring the first Catholic missionaries, the unveiling of a commemorative plaque and the blessing of an altar by Archbishop Loy Chong.

He said the occasion brought together different Christian traditions to honour missionaries who settled on Lakeba in 1844, while highlighting the importance of maintaining unity within communities bound by village, family and tradition.

item.title: Police probe man’s death
item.description: POLICE are investigating the death of a man whose body was found outside the Lautoka Post Office on Tavewa Ave yesterday. Criminal Investigations Department (CID) officers transported the body in a body bag to the Lautoka Aspen Hospital mortuary.
item.content:encoded:
POLICE are investigating the death of a man whose body was found outside the Lautoka Post Office on Tavewa Ave yesterday.

Criminal Investigations Department (CID) officers transported the body in a body bag to the Lautoka Aspen Hospital mortuary.

Police said the deceased was a known street dweller and was found by a 45-year-old man who reported the matter to police.

“A post-mortem examination will be conducted to ascertain the cause of death of a man found motionless in Lautoka City this morning (yesterday),” police said in a statement.

The cause of death has not been established.

Meanwhile, Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection Sashi Kiran said she was not aware of the incident but would comment later.

item.title: Judge says COI biased
item.description: HIGH Court judge Justice Dane Tuiqereqere found that the FICAC Commissioner of Inquiry Justice David Ashton-Lewis had “apparently made up his mind” about improper interference in the appointment of Barbara Malimali before hearing the evidence. The finding is contained in Justice Tuiqereqere’s 154-page judgment quashing the findings of the Commission of Inquiry, which was established in 2024 to inq
item.content:encoded:
HIGH Court judge Justice Dane Tuiqereqere found that the FICAC Commissioner of Inquiry Justice David Ashton-Lewis had “apparently made up his mind” about improper interference in the appointment of Barbara Malimali before hearing the evidence.

The finding is contained in Justice Tuiqereqere’s 154-page judgment quashing the findings of the Commission of Inquiry, which was established in 2024 to inquire into whether there had been improper interference in Ms Malimali’s appointment as commissioner of the Fiji Independent Commission Against Corruption.

Justice Tuiqereqere considered whether remarks made by Justice Ashton-Lewis could lead a fair-minded and fully informed observer to apprehend that he had not brought an impartial mind to the inquiry.

“The test is objective,” Justice Tuiqereqere said.

“The test is considered from the point of view of the fair-minded fully informed observer.”

Justice Tuiqereqere said he was satisfied that the test for apparent bias had been met.

“I am satisfied that a fair-minded fully informed observer would arrive at the conclusion of apparent bias on the part of Justice Ashton-Lewis,” he said.

The judge specifically referred to Justice Ashton-Lewis’ numerous references to looking for “crocodiles in the pond” during the inquiry.

Justice Tuiqereqere said a fair-minded observer could interpret those remarks as indicating that Justice Ashton-Lewis believed from the outset that there were people who had interfered in Ms Malimali’s appointment and that his role was to identify them.

“The analogy to crocodiles appears to refer to interference in the appointment of Ms Malimali and Justice Ashton-Lewis apparently saw his task as identifying and naming those who had interfered,” he said.

Justice Tuiqereqere concluded that a fair-minded and fully informed observer would not have confidence that the Commissioner had retained an open and impartial mind on whether interference had actually occurred.

He said Justice Ashton-Lewis had “apparently already made up his mind that interference existed”.

The High Court did not find sufficient evidence to establish actual bias on Justice Ashton-Lewis, but found there was sufficient basis to establish apparent bias — whether a fair-minded and informed observer could reasonably apprehend a lack of impartiality.

The apparent bias finding was among several grounds considered by the High Court in its decision to quash the COI findings.

item.title: Man dies in freak railway accident
item.description: POLICE are investigating the death of a man in his late 20s from Vunika, Labasa, following an accident along the Vou tramline yesterday morning. The incident allegedly involved a locomotive, with police questioning a 58-year-old locomotive driver and his co-driver.
item.content:encoded:
POLICE are investigating the death of a man in his late 20s from Vunika, Labasa, following an accident along the Vou tramline yesterday morning.

The incident allegedly involved a locomotive, with police questioning a 58-year-old locomotive driver and his co-driver.

“The circumstances surrounding the incident are still under investigation,” police said in a statement.

A post-mortem examination will be conducted to determine the cause of death.

Police are also expected to continue interviewing people who may have information relevant to the investigation.

item.title: Airports manager wins international procurement award
item.description: Fiji Airports Ltd has received the Chartered Institute of Procurement and Supply (CPIS) award in the Highly Commended in the Best Procurement Transformation and Change Program category at the 2026 CIPS ANZ Excellence in Procurement and Supply Awards in Australia. The international recognition acknowledges Fiji Airports’ transformation of procurement from a finance-embedded, largely manual stores p
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Airports Ltd has received the Chartered Institute of Procurement and Supply (CPIS) award in the Highly Commended in the Best Procurement Transformation and Change Program category at the 2026 CIPS ANZ Excellence in Procurement and Supply Awards in Australia.

The international recognition acknowledges Fiji Airports’ transformation of procurement from a finance-embedded, largely manual stores process into a board-approved standalone function that supports the organisation’s strategic priorities and billion-dollar infrastructure expansion and technological modernisation projects.

According to Fiji Airports, the transformation introduced stronger governance, improved transparency and audit readiness, enhanced supplier engagement, and established a new procurement framework under which 118 tenders had been processed.

It stated the program also resulted in the closure of 11 audit findings and strengthened procurement’s role in support the institution as it prepared to deliver a $2.3 billion infrastructure program.

Fiji Airports chief executive officer Mesake Nawari said this was the first time for an organisation from Fiji to receive a CIPS award, and demonstrated that their commitment to governance, transparency, fairness and sustainability were being recognised internationally.

He said the transformation had fundamentally changed the way procurement supported their strategic direction.

“Procurement is a strategic function that enables us to deliver world-class infrastructure, strengthen operational performance, manage risk and create long-term value for our stakeholders,” Mr Nawari said.

“This highly commended recognition validates the dedication of our procurement team and the collective commitment of our board, executive leadership team and staff to embedding international best practice across Fiji Airports.

“Fiji Airports continues to punch above its weight,” Mr Nawari said.

He said the institution now operated under a procurement policy framework designed to improve transparency, accountability and operational efficiency while supporting sustainable infrastructure investment and responsible business practices.

item.title: InsideSTORY I eDollar mobile wallet
item.description: LAST week, Bank South Pacific (BSP) Fiji launched its mobile wallet eDollar – becoming the first commercial bank in Fiji and the Pacific to have a bank-backed electronic wallet. BSP eDollar will bring the reach of its banking network directly to its customers through their mobile phones, and will allow them greater choice, control and convenience in how they manage and move their money.
item.content:encoded:
LAST week, Bank South Pacific (BSP) Fiji launched its mobile wallet eDollar – becoming the first commercial bank in Fiji and the Pacific to have a bank-backed electronic wallet.

BSP eDollar will bring the reach of its banking network directly to its customers through their mobile phones, and will allow them greater choice, control and convenience in how they manage and move their money.

The Fiji Times has established that this multi-million-dollar investment was fully funded by the bank, and the application took more than a year to build.

BSP Fiji relieving country head Maikash Ali said as banking became more digital, they were committed to ensuring no customer was left behind.

“BSP eDollar empowers our valued customers with greater access to manage their own accounts more flexibility in how they move funds plus the ability to pay by other people or businesses via QR code,” Mr Ali said.

Through the app, customers can create and manage up to five electronic wallets, each with its own unique account number and the option of domestic or international access.

Customers can move funds between their BSP accounts and e-wallets, transfer funds to other BSP customers, and transact across participating banks and mobile wallets.

“You can create five different wallets and the purpose of that is, if you want to save for travel or for your children’s school fees, food expenses, transport, etc, you can create a wallet for each, and for every fortnight or every week as you get paid, move money into each wallet,” Mr Ali said in an interview.

However, he said what made eDollar particularly meaningful was what it changed for their customers.

He said services that once required a visit to a branch, time spent in a queue, or a call to the bank’s customer service centre could increasingly be managed directly by customers from their own mobile devices.

A standout feature as well is QR payments, allowing customers to generate their own QR code for each e-wallet, enabling instant transfers between individuals and instant payments at any BSP QR merchant location.

Mr Ali said the BSP eDollar is aligned with the Reserve Bank of Fiji’s (RBF) National QR Code Standard.

“I find that the most amazing feature. For example, if you were to pay me, you’ll go straight on your e-wallet, create a QR code, and either send it to me if we are in different towns, or if we are together, you can just show it to me and I can scan it straight away, and funds can be transferred instantly between people.

“And this is also enabling or having Fiji move closer to a cashless society.”

Customers can start using this bank-backed wallet by downloading the eDollar app from Google Play Store or the App Store for Apple devices.

RBF governor Ariff Ali said the launch of BSP’s eDollar e-wallet closely aligned with the central bank’s payment system modernisation agenda that sought to build a payment system that was safe, efficient, inclusive and resilient.

He said in an increasingly digital and interconnected world, the ability to send and receive funds instantly was not a luxury but a necessity.

“Hence, modern payment infrastructure is no longer simply a convenience, it is the cornerstone of the financial sector and an essential component of economic development,” the governor said.

He said a key part of the modernisation journey was interoperability where customers and businesses could transact more easily across providers, platforms and channels.

“Interoperability creates a level playing field, rather than building separate and closed payment ecosystems.

“In support of this, the RBF recently introduced a National QR Code Standard, developed with industry input to promote consistency and interoperability across QR payment solutions.”

He said eDollar incorporated Fiji’s National QR Standard, making it interoperable with other participating payment service providers.

“This is a major milestone because interoperability lies at the heart of an efficient payment ecosystem.

“It enables customers to make payments seamlessly, regardless of the institution or payment application they use, while giving merchants confidence that they can accept payments from multiple providers through a single QR code.

“This is exactly the type of open, connected and competitive payments ecosystem that Fiji has been working towards.”

With the convenience in banking now accessible via this mobile wallet, the bank has advised came with a shared responsibility.

The bank’s relieving country head said they had advised every customer to treat their eDollar wallets with the same care they would give their bank account.

He urged customers to stay alert to unsolicited calls or messages asking for personal or account details, and to contact the bank immediately if anything ever felt out of place.

“An e-wallet should feel effortless to use and safe to trust. That is a standard we hold ourselves to every day,” Mr Ali said.

He said as there was more and more offerings, criminals were trying to steal customer credentials by creating fake sites.
